# Adjudication Task — Chapter 232

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃232화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|단신인 적천강과 달리, 법왕(法王) 굉도는 훌쩍 큰 키의 노인이었다.
  6|
  7|눈빛에는 장난기가 가득했고 산길을 오르는 발걸음에는 힘이 넘쳤다.
  8|
  9|‘그런데 어딜 가는 거지?’
 10|
 11|잘 닦인 길을 놔두고 도통 사람이 지나가지 않을 곳만 골라서 가니 그런 의문이 드는 것은 당연했다.
 12|
 13|그렇게 얼마나 걸었을까, 마침내 굉도의 발걸음이 멈췄다.
 14|
 15|“귀한 곳에 누추한 객들이 왔군. 부담되겠지만 사양 말고 들어오게.”
 16|
 17|‘귀한 곳’을 물끄러미 바라보던 적천강이 입을 열었다.
 18|
 19|“자네 혹시 소림사에서 쫓겨나기라도 했나?”
 20|
 21|“응? 왜?”
 22|
 23|“몰라서 물어보나? 처소 꼬락서니가 왜 이 모양이야?”
 24|
 25|적천강의 말처럼 무성한 잡초와 나무가 둘러싸고 있는 그곳은, 무림의 태산북두인 소림사의 방장이자 법왕의 거처라고 하기에는 너무 초라해 보였다.
 26|
 27|“솔직히 말해. 소림사 방장, 잘렸지?”
 28|
 29|아니, 무슨 소림사 방장이 편의점 알바도 아니고.
 30|
 31|적천강의 말에 어이가 없어진 내가 물었다.
 32|
 33|“그게 잘릴 수도 있는 겁니까?”
 34|
 35|“이런 편협한 놈을 보았나, 반란으로 황제도 끌어내리는데 소림사라고 안 될 것이 있느냐?”
 36|
 37|“…….”
 38|
 39|그렇게 나오니 할 말이 없긴 하다.
 40|
 41|막상 나도 현대에서는 몬스터 때려잡던 놈인데 뭘. 이쪽은 마왕이니 게이트니 하는 마당에 소림사 방장이 비정규직일 수도 있지.
 42|
 43|우리의 문답을 들은 굉도가 허허 웃었다.
 44|
 45|“내가 있는 곳이 방장실이지. 우리 소림사는 그런 격식 안 따진다네. 안 그러냐, 제자야?”
 46|
 47|무명이 대답했다.
 48|
 49|“계율원(戒律院)의 간청도 무시하고 이곳에 머무르는 중이십니다.”
 50|
 51|“…….”
 52|
 53|누구 친구 아니랄까 봐, 저 양반도 만만치 않구나.
 54|
 55|그러나 굉도는 껄껄 웃으며 품에서 웬 지팡이를 꺼내어 흔들어 보였다.
 56|
 57|“제 놈들이 별수 있나. 괜히 안 한다는 사람한테 방장 직을 맡긴 게 누군데?”
 58|
 59|그것은 턱없이 짧은 지팡이였다. 얼마나 많은 손길을 스쳤는지 윤활유라도 바른 것처럼 반들반들한 표면에는 은은한 녹색 빛이 감돌았다.
 60|
 61|‘거기다가 이상하게 생긴 돌까지 박혀 있고.’
 62|
 63|어찌 보면 마법사들이 쓰는 스태프와 비슷한 형태.
 64|
 65|하지만 굉도의 녹색 지팡이는 뭔가 달랐다. 세월의 흔적에 더해서 그것만이 가질 수 있는 고유한 기운이 느껴졌다.
 66|
 67|‘저게 뭐지?’
 68|
 69|의문은 다음 순간 풀렸다.
 70|
 71|“녹옥불장(綠玉佛杖). 막중한 권위를 지닌 천년 소림의 신물을 이런 땡중에게 맡기다니. 다들 눈이 단단히 삔 게지.”
 72|
 73|적천강이 쯧쯧 혀를 찼다.
 74|
 75|“소림사 꼴 잘 돌아간다.”
 76|
 77|“문도라고 해 봤자 제자 하나밖에 없는 열화문보다야 훨씬 낫지.”
 78|
 79|“뭣이라!”
 80|
 81|“불같은 성정은 여전하구먼. 부디 내세(來世)에는 선하고 침착한 이로 태어나시게.”
 82|
 83|“내세라니! 아직 멀쩡한데 왜 벌써 죽여!”
 84|
 85|“허어, 시체가 말도 하는구나. 아미타불.”
 86|
 87|“굉도, 이 땡중아!”
 88|
 89|티격태격하며 법당(法堂)으로 들어가는 두 사람의 뒷모습을 바라보다 고개를 돌렸다.
 90|
 91|무명이 빙긋 웃으며 나를 바라보고 있었다.
 92|
 93|“두 분 다 오랜만에 친우를 만나 기분이 좋으신 것 같습니다.”
 94|
 95|“……어떻게 친해졌는지 감이 잘 안 잡히는데요.”
 96|
 97|소림사의 괴짜 방장과 성질 더러운 열화문의 문주라.
 98|
 99|성격은 얼추 맞는다 쳐도 친해질 만한 조합은 아니다. 더군다나 적천강은 불교에서 금한다는 살생을 숱하게 저지른 인물 아닌가.
100|
101|내 떨떠름한 말에 뭔가를 곰곰이 생각하던 무명이 번쩍거리는 이마를 탁, 쳤다.
102|
103|“아, 기억났습니다.”
104|
105|“깜짝이야, 태양권 쓰는 줄…… 근데 뭐가요?”
106|
107|“두 분이 친해지신 계기 말입니다. 정마대전 당시 스승님께서 몰래 술과 고기를 먹고 계셨는데, 적 시주께 들킨 후로 술친구가 되셨다고 합니다.”
108|
109|“예?”
110|
111|순간 그런 생각이 들었다.
112|
113|내 귀가 잘못됐나, 하는 생각이.
114|
115|“술과 고기를 드셨다고요?”
116|
117|“예.”
118|
119|“그때도 소림사 방장 아니셨어요?”
120|
121|“맞습니다.”
122|
123|“아, 여기 스님들께서는 고기를 드시는구나. 하긴 무공 익히시면서 벌크업도 하셔야 하니까 당연히…….”
124|
125|“그건 아닙니다만. 불가(佛家)에서는 살생을 금하고 있습니다. 가축도 예외는 아니지요.”
126|
127|“……?”
128|
129|“……?”
130|
131|이거 뭐가 어디서부터 잘못된 거냐.
132|
133|나는 한동안 말을 잇지 못하고 무명을 멍하니 바라봤다.
134|
135|그리고 그의 헐렁한 승복 안에서 꿈틀거리는 근육들을 보며 확신했다.
136|
137|‘이 자식도 고기 먹는구나.’
138|
139|저 근육 봐라. 절간 산채비빔밥 정도로 키울 수 있는 피지컬이 아니다.
140|
141|심심하면 돼지 한 마리 굽고 비빔밥을 먹어도 육회 비빔밥으로 먹어야 가능하지.
142|
143|‘소림사가 아니라 주지육림사였구나.’
144|
145|무림은 한 치 앞을 예상할 수 없다던 누군가의 말이 딱 맞다.
146|
147|나는 고개를 저으며 두 사람의 뒤를 따라 불당으로 발을 디뎠다.
148|
149|
150|
151|* * *
152|
153|
154|
155|불당 내부는 좁고 오래됐지만 고풍스러운 멋이 있었다.
156|
157|먼지 하나 없이 깨끗한 바닥과 크고 작은 불상들.
158|
159|무명은 잠시 자리를 비웠고, 나와 적천강, 굉도는 마주 보고 앉아 찻잔을 비웠다. 이름 모를 풀로 우려낸 그것은 떫고 씁쓸했다.
160|
161|“귀빈 대접이 말이 아니군. 이게 뭔가?”
162|
163|“뭐긴. 내가 직접 농사지은 찻잎이지.”
164|
165|“찻잎? 자네가?”
166|
167|“나이도 먹을 만큼 먹었으니 곡차(穀茶)도 끊어야지. 벌써 수십 년 되었네.”
168|
169|“…….”
170|
171|그런 것치고는 이미 술을 먹을 만큼 먹은 것 같은데.
172|
173|차마 말은 못 하고 찻잔만 기울이는 나와 달리 적천강은 입을 딱 벌렸다.
174|
175|“어디 아픈가? 죽을병에라도 걸렸어?”
176|
177|“죽을병이라, 그럴 수도 있고 아닐 수도 있겠지. 나도 잘 모르겠네.”
178|
179|태연한 대답이었지만 무슨 이유에선지 적천강의 얼굴은 딱딱하게 굳었다.
180|
181|“그 말은 혹시…….”
182|
183|“그 이야기는 나중에 하세.”
184|
185|가볍게 손을 내저어 말을 끊어 낸 굉도가 고개를 돌려 나를 빤히 응시했다.
186|
187|“자, 그래서…… 시주가 바로 그 신성(新星)의 주인인가?”
188|
189|신성의 주인.
190|
191|반나절 전, 무명의 입을 통해 처음 들었던 단어다.
192|
193|아마 무림에 신성이 나타났니, 뭐니 하는 호사가들의 소문이 입을 타고 전해진 모양이다.
194|
195|‘벌써 여기까지 소문이 났나.’
196|
197|산서잠룡이라는 별호가 요즘 나날이 떡상 중이긴 하지만 소림 방장까지 알아볼 줄은 몰랐다.
198|
199|졸지에 월드 클래스가 된 나는 멋쩍게 웃어 보였다.
200|
201|“과찬이십니다. 아직 그 정도는 아닌걸요.”
202|
203|“보기보다 말귀가 어둡군.”
204|
205|“예?”
206|
207|“빈승이 신성의 주인이라 하지 않았나.”
208|
209|아니, 그래서 그게 뭔데.
210|
211|어리둥절한 나를 보며 굉도가 빙긋 웃었다.
212|
213|“시주, 신성이 무엇인지 알고 있는가?”
214|
215|“어, 그게. 보통은 두각을 드러내는 사람들을 신성이라고 부르지 않나요?”
216|
217|“그리고?”
218|
219|“……별?”
220|
221|“바로 맞췄네.”
222|
223|고개를 끄덕인 굉도가 잔잔한 목소리로 말을 이어 갔다.
224|
225|“빈승은 아주 오래전부터 하늘을 관찰해 왔지. 아주 헛된 공부는 아니었는지 천기(天氣)를 제법 보고 읽을 수 있게 되었네.”
226|
227|“천기…….”
228|
229|문득 지난 반나절 간의 사건이 뇌리를 스쳤다.
230|
231|무명. 그는 스승인 굉도의 지시에 따라 우리를 찾아왔고, 나를 보자마자 신성의 주인이라는 단어를 입에 올렸다.
232|
233|그리고 적천강이 뭐랬더라? 아, 그래.
234|
235|
236|
237|‘신통한 땡중 같으니. 앉아서 천 리를 내다보는 건 여전하군.’
238|
239|
240|
241|그건 사람을 통한 정보가 아니라, 바로 그 천기를 읽어서 우리를 인도했다는 뜻이었다.
242|
243|‘만약 그게 사실이라면 사이비 점쟁이 수준은 절대 아닌데.’
244|
245|아니, 오히려 예언이라 불려도 손색이 없다.
246|
247|굉도에게서 심상치 않은 기색을 느낀 나는 침을 꿀꺽 삼켰다.
248|
249|“그래서요?”
250|
251|“신성은 폭죽과도 같은 별일세. 밤하늘을 환하게 밝혔다가, 시간이 지나면 희미해지지. 하나 이번만큼은 달랐어.”
252|
253|굉도의 손가락이 불당의 문밖을 향했다. 그가 가리키는 곳은 산서성이 있는 북쪽 저 너머였다.
254|
255|“어느 날, 북쪽에서 새로운 신성이 떠올랐네. 그리고 그 신성은 지금까지도 빛이 사그라지지 않았지. 아니, 날이 갈수록 그 밝기를 더해 가고 있네.”
256|
257|“…….”
258|
259|“세인들은 종종 사람과 별을 빗대어 말하고는 하지. 빈승은 그 신성을 자네라고 생각하네.”
260|
261|위대한 업적을 이룬 누군가가 태어나고 죽을 때마다 사람들은 기뻐하고 탄식한다.
262|
263|새로운 별이 떠올랐다. 혹은 큰 별이 떨어졌다고.
264|
265|‘그런데 이번에 나타난 신성이 나를 가리킨다고?’
266|
267|굉도의 말뜻을 해석해 보면 좋은 뜻인 건 분명하다.
268|
269|하지만 글쎄, 나는 잘 모르겠다.
270|
271|아리송한 표정으로 뒤통수를 긁적이던 그때. 굉도의 한마디가 귓가를 파고들었다.
272|
273|“그때가 넉 달 전이었지.”
274|
275|“……!”
276|
277|순간 전기에 감전된 것처럼 전신이 찌릿했다.
278|
279|입이 바싹 마르고 심장이 쿵쾅거린다. 머릿속에서는 한 단어만이 빙글빙글 돌았다.
280|
281|‘넉 달 전이라고?’
282|
283|그때라면…… 내가 막 무림에서 눈을 떴을 시기다.
284|
285|마른침만 꿀꺽 삼키는 나를 향해 굉도가 빙그레 웃었다.
286|
287|“짚이는 게 있는가 보군.”
288|
289|“아, 아, 아뇨. 전혀.”
290|
291|잠자코 이야기를 듣고 있던 적천강이 한심하다는 표정으로 끼어들었다.
292|
293|“다 티 난다, 이놈아.”
294|
295|“지, 진짜 아닌데요.”
296|
297|“어쭈? 저 혓바닥을 확, 그냥.”
298|
299|“왜, 왜 이러세요.”
300|
301|젠장, 자꾸 혀가 꼬이네.
302|
303|적천강의 매서운 눈초리를 피해 슬금슬금 엉덩이를 빼는 내 모습에 굉도가 껄껄 웃었다.
304|
305|“시주가 뒷간이 급한 모양이군. 이만 나가 보아도 좋네.”
306|
307|“가라. 뒷간에 처박히고 싶으면.”
308|
309|나는 두 사람을 번갈아 보다가 문을 향해 냅다 뛰었다.
310|
311|등 뒤로 굉도의 박장대소와 적천강의 고함이 들려왔다.
312|
313|
314|
315|* * *
316|
317|
318|
319|“으하, 으하하!”
320|
321|“버르장머리 없는 놈 같으니. 감히 스승이 말하는데…….”
322|
323|투덜거리는 적천강을 바라보던 굉도가 물었다.
324|
325|“이번에 들인 제자인가?”
326|
327|뜨끔한 적천강이 황급히 헛기침을 내뱉었다.
328|
329|“어흠. 커흐흠! 제자는 아니고. 한 수 가르쳐 달라고 하도 애걸복걸하기에 잠깐 맡은 거지 뭐. 응. 그런 걸세.”
330|
331|“그런가?”
332|
333|“아, 그렇다니까!”
334|
335|“그렇다면 그런 거지 왜 소리를 지르고 그러나? 부처님들 노하시게.”

[P174]
A poisonous aura strong enough to make his nose tingle poured from the jar. Jeok Cheongang stared in amazement.

[P175]
“Isn’t this thing lethally venomous? Where did you catch it?”

[P176]
Hong Dao gazed off toward the distant mountains.

[P177]
“While I was out for a walk.”

[P178]
“…You must have searched the whole mountain with the intention of making snake liquor from the start. There are limits to being a dirty monk. Now you’re killing things just to have a drink?”

[P179]
“If you don’t want any, never mind. I’ll drink it myself.”

[P180]
“Now, now.”

[P181]
Jeok Cheongang gave Hong Dao a pointed glare, then muttered, “Still, this thing’s venom must be no joke…”

[P182]
“Indeed. A single drop squeezed from a Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake could kill a hundred cows.”

[P183]
“It’s been in there for thirty years. At this point, that’s not liquor. It’s poison.”

[P184]
“We only broke the seal for a moment, and already this much poisonous energy has escaped. What more is there to say?”

[P185]
“Something this strong would kill even a decent master, wouldn’t it?”

[P186]
“It would be madness to drink it. We absolutely shouldn’t.”

[P187]
Their gazes met in midair.

[P188]
Then they spoke almost simultaneously.

[P189]
“Then we have to drink it.”

[P190]
“Of course. Absolutely.”

[P191]
“Surely it won’t kill us.”

[P192]
“Drink. We’re drinking it no matter what. I read the heavenly patterns, and today isn’t the day we die.”

[P193]
Both men were over a hundred years old, yet neither could escape the simple recklessness etched deep into every man’s bones.

[P194]
Before long, they were passing the jar back and forth and guzzling the liquor as though possessed.

[P195]
Half a shichen[^1] later, early darkness had settled over the mountain, and the jar was empty.

[P196]
“Ooh, that venomous tingle on the tip of the tongue gives it an incredible kick. Thanks to my Scorching Yang Qi, the poison can’t even touch me.”

[P197]
Jeok Cheongang licked up the very last drop while Hong Dao glared at him.

[P198]
Though both men numbered among the Ten Kings, a slight difference in skill still existed.

[P199]
Hong Dao had lost their contest of grappling techniques over possession of the jar and had failed to drink even half the liquor.

[P200]
“An old brute with nothing but strength. No wonder you’ve lived so long.”

[P201]
“Were you hoping I’d die?”

[P202]
“I at least expected you to clutch your stomach and roll around.”

[P203]
Pleasantly drunk, Jeok Cheongang burst into laughter.

[P204]
“That’s what the heavenly patterns said, isn’t it? What can we do when Heaven itself has decided our lifespans?”

[P205]
“The heavenly patterns…”

[P206]
Hong Dao murmured the words, then casually added, “That was a lie.”

[P207]
“Hm? What do you mean?”

[P208]
“Exactly what I said. I’ve been slowly going blind for the past thirty years.”

[P209]
“W-wait. Are you saying you can no longer read the heavenly patterns?”

[P210]
Hong Dao nodded silently, and Jeok Cheongang’s heart sank.

[P211]
“How did it happen? Is it because of your age?”

[P212]
“At first, I thought so too. But I was mistaken. I gave up the liquor I loved so much and secluded myself in the wilderness to calm my mind, yet nothing changed.”

[P213]
“Then…”

[P214]
“It isn’t because this old man’s faculties have grown dull.”

[P215]
Hong Dao sighed and raised his head.

[P216]
Though the ceiling of the Buddha hall blocked his view, the old monk’s profound gaze seemed to pierce straight through it.

[P217]
“The heavenly patterns are falling into disarray. The disturbance is drawing closer, faster and faster.”

[P218]
“…!”

[P219]
“Then, amid all that, a Morning Star rose. Even in those chaotic heavens, its light was unmistakably clear.”

[P220]
Jeok Cheongang’s eyelids trembled.

[P221]
“And?”

[P222]
Hong Dao considered the question for a long moment, then shook his head.

[P223]
“That is all I can say. Though the heavenly patterns are in turmoil, they still retain their form, and the great trees rooted throughout the realm will not be easily shaken. However…”

[P224]
An inscrutable light entered Hong Dao’s eyes.

[P225]
The words that followed carried the wisdom of a sage—of the current Abbot of Shaolin, the sect hailed for a thousand years as the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim, and of a man deeply versed in the study of the heavens.

[P226]
“An unknown calamity is approaching. Dark clouds will roll in from somewhere, covering the sun and swallowing the stars.”

[P227]
A sky steeped in darkness, without a single ray of light.

[P228]
Imagining it, Jeok Cheongang let one word slip out like a groan.

[P229]
“Dark Heaven?”

[P230]
“Dark Heaven. Yes, it will become just as you said—”

[P231]
Jeok Cheongang hastily cut him off.

[P232]
“No, that’s not what I meant. I remembered something Jin Wikyung, the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, told me.”

[P233]
“Jin Wikyung? I don’t know the name, but are you saying he foresaw this situation as well?”

[P234]
“More accurately, they appeared before his family. I saw the evidence with my own eyes.”

[P235]
Jeok Cheongang gave Hong Dao a detailed account of what had happened seven days and nights earlier, just before he left the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

[P236]
He told him about the surviving remnants of the Head Elder’s faction, who remained bound by the restrictions placed upon them, and everything they had learned so far. He also described the mysterious Temporary Strength Pill he had taken from Pung Yang, the Red Wind Band Leader.

[P237]
Jin Wikyung had told Jeok Cheongang everything he knew, and now Jeok Cheongang passed it all on to Hong Dao.

[P238]
“It was astonishing. The restrictions placed on them were so complex that even I couldn’t easily break them, and the effects of that Temporary Strength Pill were bizarrely powerful.”

[P239]
“To think such a thing happened…”

[P240]
“The hidden force that manipulated the Blade of Flowers from the shadows for decades. They are Dark Heaven.”

[P241]
“Hah…”

[P242]
When the story ended, Hong Dao let out a low groan and sank into thought.

[P243]
A long time passed before he finally spoke.

[P244]
“Leave immediately.”

[P245]
“…!”

[P246]
“It seems the time has come for each of us to do what we must. I will devote all my strength to preparing for this calamity, and you…”

[P247]
Jeok Cheongang gazed deeply at his old friend and finished the sentence.

[P248]
“I must stay beside the Morning Star. Make sure its light isn’t easily extinguished.”

[P249]
Jeok Cheongang knew his task did not end there. He had to protect that light while helping it shine even brighter.

[P250]
Having realized their respective duties, neither man hesitated any longer.

[P251]
“I’ll be going.”

[P252]
“I won’t see you off. We’ll save the rest of our reunion for another time.”

[P253]
Their separation had been long, and their reunion short.

[P254]
Jeok Cheongang smiled at Hong Dao one last time, then strode out of the Buddha hall without hesitation.

[P255]
As he left, he recalled the words he had never gotten the chance to say.

[P256]
*It was a short reunion, but I enjoyed it.*

[P257]
Late that night, the young man and the old man left Shaoshi Peak on Mount Song.

[P258]
They continued walking until the sun rose and set once more.

[P259]
[^1]: A *shichen* is a traditional time unit of approximately two hours.
```

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{
"chapter": 1,
"decisions": [
{
"hunk_id": "H001",
"decision": "SOL",
"reason": "brief specific reason"
},
{

},

}

}

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 232

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃232화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|단신인 적천강과 달리, 법왕(法王) 굉도는 훌쩍 큰 키의 노인이었다.
  6|
  7|눈빛에는 장난기가 가득했고 산길을 오르는 발걸음에는 힘이 넘쳤다.
  8|
  9|‘그런데 어딜 가는 거지?’
 10|
 11|잘 닦인 길을 놔두고 도통 사람이 지나가지 않을 곳만 골라서 가니 그런 의문이 드는 것은 당연했다.
 12|
 13|그렇게 얼마나 걸었을까, 마침내 굉도의 발걸음이 멈췄다.
 14|
 15|“귀한 곳에 누추한 객들이 왔군. 부담되겠지만 사양 말고 들어오게.”
 16|
 17|‘귀한 곳’을 물끄러미 바라보던 적천강이 입을 열었다.
 18|
 19|“자네 혹시 소림사에서 쫓겨나기라도 했나?”
 20|
 21|“응? 왜?”
 22|
 23|“몰라서 물어보나? 처소 꼬락서니가 왜 이 모양이야?”
 24|
 25|적천강의 말처럼 무성한 잡초와 나무가 둘러싸고 있는 그곳은, 무림의 태산북두인 소림사의 방장이자 법왕의 거처라고 하기에는 너무 초라해 보였다.
 26|
 27|“솔직히 말해. 소림사 방장, 잘렸지?”
 28|
 29|아니, 무슨 소림사 방장이 편의점 알바도 아니고.
 30|
 31|적천강의 말에 어이가 없어진 내가 물었다.
 32|
 33|“그게 잘릴 수도 있는 겁니까?”
 34|
 35|“이런 편협한 놈을 보았나, 반란으로 황제도 끌어내리는데 소림사라고 안 될 것이 있느냐?”
 36|
 37|“…….”
 38|
 39|그렇게 나오니 할 말이 없긴 하다.
 40|
 41|막상 나도 현대에서는 몬스터 때려잡던 놈인데 뭘. 이쪽은 마왕이니 게이트니 하는 마당에 소림사 방장이 비정규직일 수도 있지.
 42|
 43|우리의 문답을 들은 굉도가 허허 웃었다.
 44|
 45|“내가 있는 곳이 방장실이지. 우리 소림사는 그런 격식 안 따진다네. 안 그러냐, 제자야?”
 46|
 47|무명이 대답했다.
 48|
 49|“계율원(戒律院)의 간청도 무시하고 이곳에 머무르는 중이십니다.”
 50|
 51|“…….”
 52|
 53|누구 친구 아니랄까 봐, 저 양반도 만만치 않구나.
 54|
 55|그러나 굉도는 껄껄 웃으며 품에서 웬 지팡이를 꺼내어 흔들어 보였다.
 56|
 57|“제 놈들이 별수 있나. 괜히 안 한다는 사람한테 방장 직을 맡긴 게 누군데?”
 58|
 59|그것은 턱없이 짧은 지팡이였다. 얼마나 많은 손길을 스쳤는지 윤활유라도 바른 것처럼 반들반들한 표면에는 은은한 녹색 빛이 감돌았다.
 60|
 61|‘거기다가 이상하게 생긴 돌까지 박혀 있고.’
 62|
 63|어찌 보면 마법사들이 쓰는 스태프와 비슷한 형태.
 64|
 65|하지만 굉도의 녹색 지팡이는 뭔가 달랐다. 세월의 흔적에 더해서 그것만이 가질 수 있는 고유한 기운이 느껴졌다.
 66|
 67|‘저게 뭐지?’
 68|
 69|의문은 다음 순간 풀렸다.
 70|
 71|“녹옥불장(綠玉佛杖). 막중한 권위를 지닌 천년 소림의 신물을 이런 땡중에게 맡기다니. 다들 눈이 단단히 삔 게지.”
 72|
 73|적천강이 쯧쯧 혀를 찼다.
 74|
 75|“소림사 꼴 잘 돌아간다.”
 76|
 77|“문도라고 해 봤자 제자 하나밖에 없는 열화문보다야 훨씬 낫지.”
 78|
 79|“뭣이라!”
 80|
 81|“불같은 성정은 여전하구먼. 부디 내세(來世)에는 선하고 침착한 이로 태어나시게.”
 82|
 83|“내세라니! 아직 멀쩡한데 왜 벌써 죽여!”
 84|
 85|“허어, 시체가 말도 하는구나. 아미타불.”
 86|
 87|“굉도, 이 땡중아!”
 88|
 89|티격태격하며 법당(法堂)으로 들어가는 두 사람의 뒷모습을 바라보다 고개를 돌렸다.
 90|
 91|무명이 빙긋 웃으며 나를 바라보고 있었다.
 92|
 93|“두 분 다 오랜만에 친우를 만나 기분이 좋으신 것 같습니다.”
 94|
 95|“……어떻게 친해졌는지 감이 잘 안 잡히는데요.”
 96|
 97|소림사의 괴짜 방장과 성질 더러운 열화문의 문주라.
 98|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{
"chapter": 1,
"decisions": [
{
"hunk_id": "H001",

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
